---
name: "Objection: Hong–Page diversity loss"
about: Selected high-competence groups can underperform diverse groups
title: "[Objection] Hong–Page: "
labels: objection, hong-page, diversity
---

Hong & Page (2004) show that a selected group of individually high-ability
problem solvers can be outperformed by a more diverse group when the selected
group's errors are correlated. The paper's defense is domain-limited standing
plus correlated-error penalties (groupthink term in the simulation, E3) and
mandatory re-certification. If you believe the defense fails:

**The objection, in your own words:**

> ...

**Where does the defense fail?**

- [ ] Test-based selection necessarily correlates errors even within a domain
- [ ] The groupthink parameter (beta) is an assumption, not a finding
- [ ] Re-certification doesn't diversify; it homogenizes further
- [ ] The E3 pool-size sweep doesn't capture real-world selection dynamics
- [ ] Other:

**What evidence or experiment would change your mind?**

**Your proposed counter-design:**

*(Paper sections to start from: 5.2 and E3 results. If you challenge the
groupthink parameter, propose a calibration. That is a testable claim.)*
